lessons.title: Venn Diagram Basics
lessons.concept: Venn diagrams represent relationships between sets using overlapping circles. They help visualize common elements (intersections), total elements (unions), and elements belonging to only one set.
lessons.formula: For two sets A and B: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B). Only A = n(A) - n(A ∩ B).
lessons.worked_example: In a class, 20 like Math, 15 like Science, and 5 like both. Total who like at least one = 20 + 15 - 5 = 30. Only Math = 20 - 5 = 15.
mistakes: Adding both sets without subtracting the intersection (double counting)
Confusing 'only A' with total in A
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Two-Set Venn Problems
lessons.concept: Two-set problems typically involve people/items belonging to category A, category B, both, or neither. Draw two overlapping circles and fill regions step by step, starting from the intersection when possible.
lessons.formula: Neither = Total - n(A ∪ B). n(A ∩ B) can be found if total, A, B, and neither (or union) are known.
lessons.worked_example: Out of 50 students, 30 play cricket, 25 play football, and 10 play both. Union = 30+25-10 = 45. Neither = 50-45 = 5.
mistakes: Placing the 'both' value in the wrong region
Forgetting to account for 'neither' in total
Not subtracting intersection when computing only-one regions
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Three-Set Venn Intro
lessons.concept: Three-set diagrams use three overlapping circles creating regions for only A, only B, only C, pairwise intersections, and intersection of all three. Fill from the innermost region (all three) outward to avoid double counting.
lessons.worked_example: If 8 like all three subjects, record 8 in the center first. Then for those who like A and B (say 12 total), only A&B region = 12 - 8 = 4.
mistakes: Treating pairwise intersection values as only-two regions without removing the all-three overlap
Filling regions in random order causing inconsistencies
Double counting elements in multiple intersections

practice.question: Two sets that have no elements in common are called:
practice.explanation: Disjoint sets have an empty intersection (A intersection B = empty). Intersecting sets share at least one element.

questions.question: How is the statement 'All A are B' represented in a Venn diagram?
questions.explanation: 'All A are B' means every element of A is also in B, so the A circle is drawn completely within the B circle.
